```{r}
#| label: Physiological parameters
#| message: false
#| include: false
#| warnings: false

Physio_params <- read_csv("C:/Users/pacho003/OneDrive - Wageningen University & Research/CP_L_R/PARC_PFAS_PBPKmodel/Codes_PFAS_models/Chrysanthi_Pachoulide_2024_PFOA_mechanistic/Input/PhysioVariables.csv", show_col_types = FALSE
)

Physio_params <- Physio_params %>% 
  filter(age == 60) %>% # 60 years old adult, male
  select(ends_with('_M')) %>% 
  mutate(BloodFlowSum = rowSums(select(., starts_with("Q_")))) %>% # 0.9935; total blood flow as the sum of the fractional blood flows of all organs on which we have data
  mutate(VolumesSum = rowSums(select(., starts_with("V_")))) # 0.96; total volume as the sum of the fractional organ volumes of all organs on which we have data

BW <- Physio_params$BDW_M 
QC <- Physio_params$CardOut_M # This is corrected for hematocrit already so it's plasma

# Fractional organ volumes
VAc <- Physio_params$V_adiposeFraction_M   
MassAc <- Physio_params$AdiposeMass_M      #adipose mass
VGc <- Physio_params$V_gutFraction_M
VKc <- Physio_params$V_kidneyFraction_M
VLc <- Physio_params$V_liverFraction_M
VPc <- Physio_params$V_plasmaFraction_M
Hct <- Physio_params$Hct_M
VSkc <- Physio_params$V_skinFraction_M
VTotc <- Physio_params$VolumesSum 

# Body volumes (L)
VA <- VAc * BW/0.9 + MassAc/0.9
VG <- VGc * BW
VK <- VKc * BW
VL <- VLc * BW
VP <- VPc * (1-Hct) * BW
VSk <- VSkc * BW
VR <- (VTotc*BW) - (VA + VG + VK + VL + VP + VSk)

# Comment Chrysa about the below: it's it not clearly explained what it's meant by collecting system in ICRP. That could also be the collecting duct.
# VFil <- VK * 0.05 # 0.01557415 Kidney filtrate compartment, corresponds to the volume of the collecting system in [ICRP 89 page 149] http://www.icrp.org/publication.asp?id=ICRP%20Publication%2089


# Fractional organ blood flows
QAc <- Physio_params$Q_adiposeFraction_M/Physio_params$BloodFlowSum
QGc <- Physio_params$Q_gutFraction_M/Physio_params$BloodFlowSum 
QKc <- Physio_params$Q_kidneyFraction_M/Physio_params$BloodFlowSum 
QLc <- Physio_params$Q_liverFraction_M/Physio_params$BloodFlowSum 
QSkc <- Physio_params$Q_skinFraction_M/Physio_params$BloodFlowSum 

# Body flows (L/d)
QA <- QAc * QC
QG <- QGc * QC
QK <- QKc * QC
QL <- QLc * QC
QSk <- QSkc * QC
QR <- QC - (QA + QG + QK + QL + QSk)

QUr = 0.022 * BW # L/d, Urine flow rate to the bladder 22 mL/kg BW/d [ICRP 89 page 161]
GFR = 0.18 * QK # L/d, Glomerular filtration rate 18% of total renal plasma flow [ICRP 89 page 159] http://www.icrp.org/publication.asp?id=ICRP%20Publication%2089
QT = 43.2*60*24/1000 # L/d; Tubular flow rate at the end of the PT 43.2 ml/min TFR from Scotcher et al. 2016 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejps.2016.03.018 and Pletz


```

## Tissue - Plasma Partition coefficients

Tissue-plasma partition coefficients were calculated using experimental equilibrium matrix-water distribution coefficients. Previously, tissue-plasma partition coefficients determined from *in vivo* rat studies where used, however this approach brings a lot of uncertainties in the model, due to the physiological differences between rats and humans [@Kudo2007]. Recently, equilibrium tissue distribution coefficients were derived using PFOA tissue concentrations found in healthy human forensic autopsies of different tissues. This approach could be considered more physiologically relevant, however some limitations were the sizes of the tissue samples, that might not be representative of the whole tissue concentrations, as well as the variability in blood compositions due to blood coagulation in some of the samples [@nielsen2023].

An alternative approach to defining tissue-plasma partitionn coefficients, is the mechanistic tissue-plasma partition algorithms, that use physiochemical properties (such as Kow and pKa) to predict the chemical affinities tissue components (proteins or lipids), assuming that these depend on the lipophilicity and ionisation status of the chemical. The final steady-state tissue-plasma distribution is based on the differences in composition of the different tissues and their respective volume [@rodgers2007; @utsey2020; @peyret2010]. These mechanistic approach is very useful as it relies only on physicochemical and physiological data. However, these algorithms are limited to the chemical-space for which they have been validated for, and the uncertainties of the physicochemical data provided. Indeed, there's a lot of variability in experimentally and *in silico* derived pKa for PFOA, while, given it's amphiphilic nature taking Kow as a proxy to membrane affinity for example might be incorrect.

Recently, the binding affinity of PFOA to different tissue components (membrane phospholipids, storage lipids, structural proteins, albumin, fatty-acid binding protein) was derived experimentally [@allendorf2020]. As shown in @fig-DistributionCoeffs, PFOA has high affinity for albumin and membrane phospholipids, while it's binding affinity to structural proteins and storage lipids is lower. Noticeably, PFOA has a high affinity to fatty acid binding proteins, which are mainly found in the liver and kidney. [^1]

[^1]: I think PFOA binds in the fatty acid-binding pocket of albumin, which is a specific (therefore strong) binding. Check literature on that.

```{r}
#| include: false

# PFOA Matrix/Water Distribution Coefficients ####

logML <- 3.52  # 3.52 ± 0.08 from Ebert A., Allendorf F. et al (2020), https://dx.doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.0c00175  (Liposomes composed of POPC (1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-glycero-3-phosphocholine))
logSL <- -1.37 # -1.37 ± 0.01 from Allendorf, F., Goss, K.-U. and Ulrich, N. (2021), https://doi.org/10.1002/etc.4954 (Olive oil with a high fraction of unsaturated fatty acids, Recovery 95%)
logSP <- 1.61 # 1.61 ± 0.15 from Allendorf, F., Goss, K.-U. and Ulrich, N. (2021), https://doi.org/10.1002/etc.4954  (Structural proteins from chicken breast fillet (actin & myosin 60-95%), Recovery 95%)
logALB <- 4.33 # 4.33 ± 0.05 from Allendorf, F., Goss, K.-U. and Ulrich, N. (2021), https://doi.org/10.1002/etc.4954 (BSA (fatty acid free) Molar ratio compound to BSA < 0.1 72-96h, Recovery 94%))
logFABP <- 4.3 # calculated by Allendorf, F., Goss, K.-U. and Ulrich, N. (2021), https://doi.org/10.1002/etc.4954

k_ML <- 10^logML       # neutral phospholipids:water partition coefficient
k_SP <- 10^logSP       # structural protein:water partition coefficient
k_ALB <- 10^logALB     # albumin:water partition coefficient
k_SL <- 10^logSL       # structural lipids:water partition coefficient
k_FABP <- 10^logFABP   # fatty acid-binding protein:water partition coefficient

MatrixWater.df <- data.frame(
  Component = c("Membrane phospholipids",
                "Storage lipids",
                "Structural proteins", 
                "Albumin", 
                "Fatty acid binding proteins"),
  Distribution = c(logML, logSL, logSP, logALB, logFABP))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-DistributionCoeffs
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Matrix-Water Distribution Coefficients"
#| fig-subcap: "Membrane lipids: neutral phospholipids; Storage lipids: lipids other than phospholipids; Structural proteins: actin and myosin"

MatrixWater.plot <- MatrixWater.df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Component, y = Distribution)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Distribution coefficient (log)") +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal()
MatrixWater.plot
```

Tissue-plasma partition coefficients were calculated using the above mentioned distribution coefficients. Physiological data about the relevant tissue components were taken from literature [@allendorf2020; @utsey2020]. To enable comparison of the calculated partition coefficients with the previously used *in vivo* derived ones, partition coefficients were derived for both rat and human tissues. As illustrated in @fig-PartitionCoefficients-1 significant difference between the human and rat tissue-plasma partition coefficients is only observed for the adipose and skin tissues.

On the other hand, as seen in @fig-PartitionCoefficients-3 , when comparing the rat calculated partition coefficients with those determined from the *in vivo* rat data, important differences can be observed for the brain, kidney and liver. The calculated brain-plasma partition coefficient is higher than the one derived from the *in vivo* data, while the partition coefficients for kidney and liver are lower. This is in agreement with the results of other literature data and can be expected due to the active processes involved in the biokinetics of PFOA [@allendorf2020; @nielsen2023].

Lastly, as shown in @fig-PartitionCoefficients-2 the partition coefficients calculated in this paper match those calculated in the reference paper. Further validation of these coefficients against *in vivo* human and rat data was performed previously and was therefore not repeated here [@allendorf2020]. The results of that work are found in @fig-CalculatedVsExperimentalAllendorf

Add here Susanna's work on deriving the partition coefficients based on pKa and membrane affinity.

```{r}
#| label: Calculating Partition Coefficients
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false


# Input ####
Physio.data <- read_csv("C:/Users/pacho003/OneDrive - Wageningen University & Research/CP_L_R/PARC_PFAS_PBPKmodel/Codes_PFAS_models/Chrysanthi_Pachoulide_2024_PFOA_mechanistic/Input/TissueComposition.csv")

# Human ####
Physio.dat <- Physio.data %>% 
  filter(Species == "Human") %>% 
  filter(!Tissue %in% c("Bone", "Comment", "NamingInUtsey")) %>%
  select(- c(Comment, Species)) %>%
  mutate(across(-Tissue, as.numeric))

Physio.Tissues <- Physio.dat %>% filter(!Tissue %in% c("Blood", "Plasma"))

Kp <- (Physio.Tissues$f_W +
         (k_ML*Physio.Tissues$f_ML) +
         (k_SL*Physio.Tissues$f_SL) +
         (k_SP*Physio.Tissues$f_SP) +
         (k_ALB*Physio.Tissues$f_ALB) +
         (k_FABP*Physio.Tissues$f_FABP)
) #* fup #removing fup here to be able to correctly compare with the other methods of calculating the partition coefficient 

Names <- Physio.Tissues$Tissue #%>% substr(1,2)
# Names <- paste("Kp",Names ,sep="")
Kp.df <- as.data.frame(list(Tissue = Names)) %>%
  mutate(Human = Kp) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Tissue, values_from = Human) %>% 
  mutate(Rest = (Brain*Physio_params$V_brainFraction_M +
           Heart*Physio_params$V_heartFraction_M + 
           Lung*Physio_params$V_lungFraction_M +
           Muscle*Physio_params$V_muscleFraction_M +
           Spleen*Physio_params$V_spleenFraction_M +
           Gonads*Physio_params$V_reproFraction_M
           #Bone*Physio_params$V_boneFraction_M) / (
           ) / (Physio_params$V_brainFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_heartFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_lungFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_muscleFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_spleenFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_reproFraction_M +
               Physio_params$V_boneFraction_M)  
           ) 

# Rat ####
Physio.dat.rat <- Physio.data %>% 
  filter(Species == "Rat") %>% 
  filter(!Tissue %in% c("Comment", "NamingInUtsey", "Bone")) %>%
  select(- c(Comment, Species)) %>%
  mutate(across(-Tissue, as.numeric))

Physio.Tissues.rat <- Physio.dat.rat %>% 
  filter(!Tissue %in% c("Blood", "Plasma"))

Kp.rat <- (Physio.Tissues.rat$f_W +
         (k_ML*Physio.Tissues.rat$f_ML) +
         (k_SL*Physio.Tissues.rat$f_SL) +
         (k_SP*Physio.Tissues.rat$f_SP) +
         (k_ALB*Physio.Tissues.rat$f_ALB) +
         (k_FABP*Physio.Tissues.rat$f_FABP)
) #* fup

#Fractional volumes of organs taken from Allendorf et al. DOI: 10.1002/etc.4954
  Kp.df.rat <- as.data.frame(list(Tissue = Names)) %>%
    mutate(Rat = Kp.rat) %>% 
    pivot_wider(names_from = Tissue, values_from = Rat) %>% 
    mutate(Rest = (Brain*0.0062 + 
             Heart*0.0045 + 
             Lung*0.0068 +
             Muscle*0.5207 +
             Spleen*0.0054+
             Gonads*0.0142) / (
               0.0062 +
                 0.0045 +
                 0.0068 +
                 0.5207 +
                 0.0054 +
                 0.0142))

# Calculated by Allendorf ####
Kp.Allendorf <- tibble(
  Adipose = 2.3,
  Brain = 2.3,
  Gut = 1.9,
  Heart = 1.7,
  Kidney = 2.2,
  Liver = 2.1,
  Lung = 1.9,
  Muscle = 1.8,
  Skin = 2.3,
  Spleen = 1.9,
  Gonads = 1.8) %>% 
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "Human", Adipose:Gonads) %>% 
  mutate(Rat = c(1.5, 2.1, 1.9, 1.8, 2.3, 2.2, 2.0, 1.7, 1.9, 1.9, 1.8),
         Type = "CalculatedAllendorf") %>% 
  mutate(Human = 10^Human, Rat = 10^Rat) %>%  
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Species", values_to = "Coefficient", Human:Rat) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Tissue, values_from = Coefficient)
  
  
# Experimental ####
# Comment Chrysa 10-2-2025: No adipose measured, where does adipose:plasma partition coef. come from in Loccisano?
Tissue.conc <- tibble(
  Blood = 0.132,
  Serum = 0.254,
  Brain = 0.003,
  Gut = 0.017, 
  Heart = 0.029,
  Kidney = 0.267, 
  Liver = 0.558,
  Lung = 0.039,
  Spleen = 0.015,
  Gonads = 0.018 
)

# Correcting for fraction unbound for correct comparison with the calculated data
Kp.df.Kudo <- tibble(
  Brain = Tissue.conc$Brain/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup, #correcting for fup as the calculated ones don't account for fup
  Heart = Tissue.conc$Heart/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup,
  Gut = Tissue.conc$Gut/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup,
  Kidney = Tissue.conc$Kidney/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup,
  Liver = Tissue.conc$Liver/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup, 
  Lung = Tissue.conc$Lung/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup,
  Spleen = Tissue.conc$Spleen/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup,
  Gonads = Tissue.conc$Gonads/Tissue.conc$Serum/fup
) %>% mutate(Species = "Rat", Type = "Experimental")
  
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-PartitionCoefficients
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-cap: "Tissue/Plasma Partition Coefficients"
#| fig-subcap:
#| - "Calculated Human Vs Rat"
#| - "Calculated Vs Experimental"
#| - "Calculated Vs Allendorf"


# Calculated Human Vs Rat ####

Kp.combined.df <- rbind(Kp.df, Kp.df.rat) %>% 
  mutate(Species = c("Human", "Rat"),
         Type = c("Calculated", "Calculated")) 

KpCompare.plot <- Kp.combined.df %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "Coefficient", Adipose:Rest) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Tissue, Coefficient), y = log10(Coefficient), fill = Species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Partition Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8856a7", "#af8dc3"))+
  ylab("Partition Coefficient (logK)")
KpCompare.plot


# Calculated Vs Experimental ####

Kp.CalcVsExp.df <- Kp.combined.df %>% 
  select(c(Brain, Heart, Gut, Kidney, Liver, Lung, Spleen, Gonads, Species, Type)) %>%   rbind(Kp.df.Kudo)
  
KpCalcVsExp.plot <- Kp.CalcVsExp.df %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "Coefficient", Brain:Gonads) %>% 
  filter(Species == "Rat") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Tissue, Coefficient), y = log10(Coefficient), fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Partition Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8856a7", "#3288BD")) +
  ylab("Partition Coefficient (logK)")
KpCalcVsExp.plot

KpCalcVsExp.diff <- Kp.CalcVsExp.df %>%
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "Coefficient", Brain:Gonads) %>% 
  mutate(Coefficient = log10(Coefficient)) %>% 
  filter(Species == "Rat") %>% 
  select(Type, Tissue, Coefficient) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Type, values_from = Coefficient) %>% 
  mutate(ErrorRate = abs(Calculated - Experimental)/Experimental) %>% 
  mutate(Accuracy = (1-ErrorRate)*100)


# Calculated Vs Calculated Allendorf ####

Kp.Calculated <- Kp.combined.df %>% select(!Rest)
Kp.Calc.Compare <- rbind(Kp.Calculated, Kp.Allendorf) %>% 
  pivot_longer(names_to = "Tissue", values_to = "Coefficient", Adipose:Gonads)

Kp.Calc.Compare.plot <- Kp.Calc.Compare %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Tissue, Coefficient), y = log10(Coefficient), fill = Type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~Species) +
  labs(
    x = "",
    y = "Partition Coefficient") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#8856a7", "#7fbf7b")) +
  ylab("Partition Coefficient (logK)")
Kp.Calc.Compare.plot



```

```{r}
#| label: Final Partition Coefficients
#| include: false

# Final Tissue/Plasma Partition coefficients ####
Final_Kp.df <- Kp.df %>% 
  pivot_longer(values_to = "Coefficient", names_to = "Tissue", Adipose:Rest) %>% 
  mutate(Coefficient = Coefficient*fup) %>% #correcting for fup here
  filter(Tissue %in% c("Adipose", "Gut", "Liver", "Kidney", "Skin", "Rest")) 

Final_Kp.df$Tissue <- paste("Kp", Final_Kp.df$Tissue, sep = "")
Final_Kp.df$Tissue <- substr(Final_Kp.df$Tissue, 1,4)

```
